# ztfttr

> Copies a triangular matrix from Rectangular Full Packed (RFP) format to standard full format.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import ztfttr from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/ztfttr';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
ztfttr( order, transr, uplo, N, ARF, strideARF, A, LDA ) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout (`'row-major'` or `'column-major'`) |
| `transr` | `"no-transpose" \| "conjugate-transpose"` | Specifies whether `ARF` is in normal or conjugate-transpose format (`'no-transpose'` or `'conjugate-transpose'`) |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | Specifies whether the matrix is upper or lower triangular (`'upper'` or `'lower'`) |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `ARF` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length trunc(N * (N + 1) / 2)</sub> | Input array in RFP format |
| ↳ `strideARF` | `integer` | Stride length for `ARF` |
| `A` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **out** · Output matrix in full format |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `A`<br>Requires `LDA ≥ max(1, N)` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `transr`:

  -   `= 'N'`: `ARF` is in Normal format;
  -   `= 'C'`: `ARF` is in Conjugate-transpose format;
- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: A is upper triangular;
  -   `= 'L'`: A is lower triangular.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `ARF`: On entry, the upper or lower triangular matrix A stored in RFP format. For a further discussion see Notes below.
- `A`: On exit, the triangular matrix A. If `UPLO = 'U'`, the leading N-by-N upper triangular part of the array A contains the upper triangular matrix, and the strictly lower triangular part of A is not referenced. If `UPLO = 'L'`, the leading N-by-N lower triangular part of the array A contains the lower triangular matrix, and the strictly upper triangular part of A is not referenced.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "conjugate-transpose", "no-transpose"
- `TypeError` third argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` eighth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
ztfttr.ndarray(
    transr, uplo,
    N,
    ARF, strideARF, offsetARF,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA
) → integer
```

Copy a triangular matrix from Rectangular Full Packed format (RFP) to standard full format (TR).

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `transr` | `"no-transpose" \| "conjugate-transpose"` | Specifies whether `ARF` is in normal or conjugate-transpose format<br>One of `'conjugate-transpose'`, `'no-transpose'`. |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | Specifies whether the matrix is upper or lower triangular |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `ARF` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length trunc(N * (N + 1) / 2)</sub> | Input array in RFP format |
| ↳ `strideARF` | `integer` | Stride length for `ARF` |
| ↳ `offsetARF` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `ARF` |
| `A` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **out** · Output matrix in full format |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `A` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `transr`:

  -   `= 'N'`: `ARF` is in Normal format;
  -   `= 'C'`: `ARF` is in Conjugate-transpose format;
- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: A is upper triangular;
  -   `= 'L'`: A is lower triangular.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `ARF`: On entry, the upper or lower triangular matrix A stored in RFP format. For a further discussion see Notes below.
- `A`: On exit, the triangular matrix A. If `UPLO = 'U'`, the leading N-by-N upper triangular part of the array A contains the upper triangular matrix, and the strictly lower triangular part of A is not referenced. If `UPLO = 'L'`, the leading N-by-N lower triangular part of the array A contains the lower triangular matrix, and the strictly upper triangular part of A is not referenced.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (0 = success)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "conjugate-transpose", "no-transpose"
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value

</section>

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `ztfttr()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`ZTFTTR`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/ztfttr.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import reinterpret from '@stdlib/strided/base/reinterpret-complex128/lib/index.js';
import ztfttr from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/ztfttr';

const N = 3;

// Triangular matrix in Rectangular Full Packed (RFP) format, N*(N+1)/2 complex elements:
const ARF = new Complex128Array( [ 1.0, 0.0, 2.0, 1.0, 3.0, -1.0, 4.0, 0.0, 5.0, 2.0, 6.0, 0.0 ] );

// Using the standard interface:
let A = new Complex128Array( N * N );
ztfttr( 'row-major', 'no-transpose', 'upper', N, ARF, 1, A, N );
console.log( reinterpret( A, 0 ) ); // eslint-disable-line no-console

// Using the ndarray interface:
A = new Complex128Array( N * N );
ztfttr.ndarray( 'no-transpose', 'upper', N, ARF, 1, 0, A, N, 1, 0 );
console.log( reinterpret( A, 0 ) ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZTFTTR`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZTFTTR copies a triangular matrix A from rectangular full packed format (TF) to standard full format (TR).

### Further Details

We first consider Standard Packed Format when N is even. We give an example where $N = 6$.

```text
AP is Upper             AP is Lower
```

```text
00 01 02 03 04 05       00
   11 12 13 14 15       10 11
      22 23 24 25       20 21 22
         33 34 35       30 31 32 33
            44 45       40 41 42 43 44
               55       50 51 52 53 54 55
```

Let `TRANSR = 'N'`. RFP holds AP as follows: For `UPLO = 'U'` the upper trapezoid `A(0:5,0:2)` consists of the last three columns of AP upper. The lower triangle `A(4:6,0:2)` consists of conjugate-transpose of the first three columns of AP upper. For `UPLO = 'L'` the lower trapezoid `A(1:6,0:2)` consists of the first three columns of AP lower. The upper triangle `A(0:2,0:2)` consists of conjugate-transpose of the last three columns of AP lower. To denote conjugate we place -- above the element. This covers the case N even and `TRANSR = 'N'`.

```text
RFP A                   RFP A
```

```text
                        -- -- --
03 04 05                33 43 53
                           -- --
13 14 15                00 44 54
                              --
23 24 25                10 11 55
```

```text
33 34 35                20 21 22
--
00 44 45                30 31 32
-- --
01 11 55                40 41 42
-- -- --
02 12 22                50 51 52
```

Now let `TRANSR = 'C'`. RFP A in both `UPLO` cases is just the conjugate- transpose of RFP A above. One therefore gets:

```text
RFP A                   RFP A
```

```text
-- -- -- --                -- -- -- -- -- --
03 13 23 33 00 01 02    33 00 10 20 30 40 50
-- -- -- -- --                -- -- -- -- --
04 14 24 34 44 11 12    43 44 11 21 31 41 51
-- -- -- -- -- --                -- -- -- --
05 15 25 35 45 55 22    53 54 55 22 32 42 52
```

We next consider Standard Packed Format when N is odd. We give an example where $N = 5$.

```text
AP is Upper                 AP is Lower
```

```text
00 01 02 03 04              00
   11 12 13 14              10 11
      22 23 24              20 21 22
         33 34              30 31 32 33
            44              40 41 42 43 44
```

Let `TRANSR = 'N'`. RFP holds AP as follows: For `UPLO = 'U'` the upper trapezoid `A(0:4,0:2)` consists of the last three columns of AP upper. The lower triangle `A(3:4,0:1)` consists of conjugate-transpose of the first two columns of AP upper. For `UPLO = 'L'` the lower trapezoid `A(0:4,0:2)` consists of the first three columns of AP lower. The upper triangle `A(0:1,1:2)` consists of conjugate-transpose of the last two columns of AP lower. To denote conjugate we place -- above the element. This covers the case N odd and `TRANSR = 'N'`.

```text
RFP A                   RFP A
```

```text
                           -- --
02 03 04                00 33 43
                              --
12 13 14                10 11 44
```

```text
22 23 24                20 21 22
--
00 33 34                30 31 32
-- --
01 11 44                40 41 42
```

Now let `TRANSR = 'C'`. RFP A in both `UPLO` cases is just the conjugate- transpose of RFP A above. One therefore gets:

```text
RFP A                   RFP A
```

```text
-- -- --                   -- -- -- -- -- --
02 12 22 00 01             00 10 20 30 40 50
-- -- -- --                   -- -- -- -- --
03 13 23 33 11             33 11 21 31 41 51
-- -- -- -- --                   -- -- -- --
04 14 24 34 44             43 44 22 32 42 52
```

</section>
